title: Execution under program extension
statement: Let $L$ be a set of execution limits, let $P$ and $R$ be programs, let $d,T\in\mathbb{N}$, let $s$ be a statement, let $\sigma$ be an initial state, and let $Q$ be a predicate on states. If $s$ has an execution from $\sigma$ under $P$ at depth $d$ that ends in a state satisfying $Q$ and has cost at most $T$, then $s$ has an execution from $\sigma$ under the concatenated program $P++R$ at depth $d$ that ends in a state satisfying $Q$ and has cost at most $T$.
hypotheses_covered: An execution of $s$ from $\sigma$ under $P$ at depth $d$ ends in a state satisfying $Q$
The execution has cost at most $T$
